subject: SLA remedies, escrowed fee-at-risk, and termination triggers
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@opticore.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: OptiCore Legal <legal@opticore.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SLA remedies and remedies beyond credits

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the performance looked promising. Before we move to an internal procurement review, Legal asked that we clarify remedies for repeated SLA shortfalls. OptiCore has two specific asks: (1) a fee-at-risk / liquidated-damages-style addendum that allows us to escrow a portion of committed fees (to be released on successful SLOs), and (2) an explicit termination right if uptime/latency falls below the agreed floor for N consecutive weeks (not just credits).

We understand Redwood’s standard practice is credits-only, but given the mission-critical nature of this workload (customer-facing search) and regulatory considerations, our counsel wants an option that goes beyond credits. Can you share what flexibility you have on (a) an escrowed fee-at-risk amount (percentage, release schedule), (b) a liquidated damages cap, and (c) a termination trigger tied to repeated SLO misses?

If useful we can propose specific language. We are targeting a decision by the end of next week.

Best,
Jane
Procurement & Vendor Management
OptiCore Inc.

---
Attachment: Requirements_SLA_OptiCore_2026.xlsx (see referenced items)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@opticore.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA remedies and remedies beyond credits

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear ask and the materials. Glad the demo was helpful.

Short answer: we do not typically accept unconditional liquidated damages or termination for single/short outages; our commercial model is centered on usage credits and a graduated remedy ladder. That said, we are open to a constrained, negotiated approach for strategic customers:

- Fee-at-risk via escrow: yes, subject to limits and escrow mechanics (we have a standard escrow/invoice-hold process).
- Liquidated damages: we can consider a capped fee-at-risk that is released on successful SLO recovery; we prefer a remedial ladder (credits -> fee-withhold -> termination as last resort).
- Termination trigger: we are open to a staged termination right but only after repeated, documented SLO misses and with opportunity to remediate (can include cure windows and operational runbooks).

I’ve attached an early draft addendum with a proposed staged remedy structure and suggested caps. Rafael (security/compliance) and Neha (pricing) are on copy for input on SOC/escrow and commercial caps.

Would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the addendum line-by-line?

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: SLA_Addendum_Draft_v1.pdf (attachment)

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@opticore.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: OptiCore Legal <legal@opticore.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T08:58:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA remedies and remedies beyond credits

Lauren — thanks. Our counsel reviewed the draft and pushed back on a few items:

1) The proposed cap in v1 is too low relative to our committed spend; they want a mechanism that effectively holds 6–12 weeks of committed fees in escrow for the first year.
2) The termination path in v1 requires a long catch-up/cure period; they want a clearer trigger: if 3 out of any 6-week rolling window fall below the 99.5% uptime baseline (or equivalent latency SLO misses), OptiCore can terminate for convenience with a reduced notice.
3) They also want the addendum to state that fee-at-risk is convertible to liquidated damages (not just credits) if an incident is found to be due to persistent operational negligence.

Understand these are material asks — can you indicate whether the escrow + elevated cap + narrower termination trigger are deal breakers or negotiable? If negotiable, what alternative would Redwood accept?

-Jane

Subject: Internal: recommended counter for OptiCore escrow and termination asks

Lauren / Neha — quick thoughts from Security & Commercial:

- Escrow mechanics: we can support a 6-week fee hold in escrow for year 1 but recommend a declining schedule (6w -> 4w after year 2 -> 2w after year 3) to limit balance sheet impact and reduce ongoing risk. Require opt-in to standard escrow provider and mutually agreed release criteria. Recommend adding a clause that escrow releases automatically if Redwood meets a remediation runbook and shows root-cause analysis within 10 business days.

- Cap / liquidated damages: we will not accept open-ended conversion to liquidated damages tied to a subjective "persistent negligence" standard. Instead propose a defined threshold for negligence (e.g., repeated failure to meet runbook milestones or failure to implement agreed mitigations) and a cap equal to 3 months of committed fees in any 12-month period.

- Termination triggers: accept staged termination but only after triage, remediation window, and an independent post-mortem; propose: termination allowed after 3 qualifying SLO misses in any rolling 8-week window AND failure to remediate within 30 days following our remediation plan. This is tighter than our usual but gives them some runway and preserves operational fairness.

- Evidence: attach SOC2 summary and our monitoring export format. Legal will need to draft precise definitions and remedies.

Rafael
VP, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@opticore.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA remedies and remedies beyond credits

Jane — thanks for the concrete feedback and for sharing counsel's preferred language. We discussed internally and can offer the following counterproposal (attached as v2):

1) Escrow / fee-at-risk: Redwood will accept a 6-week escrow hold in year 1 for committed monthly fees, with a stepped reduction to 4 weeks in year 2 and 2 weeks in year 3, tied to the live subscription commitment. Funds will be held with a mutually agreed escrow agent. Release conditions: automatic release on sustained SLO compliance for the following 30 days, or manual release upon mutually agreed remediation completion and RCA.

2) Cap and conversion: We will agree to a cap of 3 months of committed fees as potential fee-at-risk/liquidated-style remedy in any 12-month period. Conversion to a monetary remedy (beyond credits) requires a defined failure-to-remediate standard (outlined in section 3 of the addendum) — i.e., failure to implement agreed mitigation milestones within prescribed windows.

3) Termination trigger: Termination for convenience tied to SLA breaches will be permitted only after:
   - Three qualifying SLO misses in any rolling 8-week window (uptime or latency as defined in the SLO table), and
   - A documented remediation notice and 30-calendar-day cure window, and
   - Completion of an independent post-mortem where the failure is attributable to operational control deficiencies (not force majeure).

We tried to balance OptiCore's need for stronger economic remedies with Redwood's operational position. Attached is v2 of the addendum with the proposed precise language, plus escrow instructions and SOC2 summary per Rafael's note. If that looks acceptable in principle, Legal can prep a DocuSign envelope and we can route to signatures.

Would you like to lock a quick legal-to-legal call today?

Thanks,
Lauren
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

If you can supply the vendor language and confirm the escalation SLA, we can route DocuSign this afternoon. Otherwise we will hold a short legal call first thing tomorrow.

I'll await the two items and then we can proceed.
